questions.title: Who will be the first person charged in the United Kingdom over alleged involvement in the 1994 Rwandan genocide?
questions.background: British authorities have been investigating allegations involving Rwandan genocide suspects living in the United Kingdom.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official public charging announcement from the United Kingdom’s Crown Prosecution Service. Resolution : Identify the first individual formally charged in the United Kingdom in connection with alleged involvement in the 1994 Rwandan genocide, provided the charges are announced by December 31, 2026. Arrests without charges, extradition proceedings, and charges brought outside the United Kingdom do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The person’s full name as given in the charging announcement.
questions.current_reasoning: Scotland Yard's War Crimes Team has investigated six Rwandan genocide suspects in the UK since 2018 and confirmed in December 2025 that two investigations are at an advanced stage with full files submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service (one submitted in late 2023, a second by late 2025), while none had been charged as of May 2026. The two CPS files almost certainly come from the four named suspects interviewed voluntarily in 2020—Celestin Mutabaruka (Kent), Celestin Ugirashebuja (Essex), Emmanuel Nteziryayo (Manchester), and Dr. Vincent Bajinya, who legally changed his name to Vincent Brown (London)—whereas fifth suspect Charles Munyaneza (Bedford) suffered a stroke and was only interviewed in 2024, and a sixth suspect arrested in Gateshead in January 2024 remains publicly unnamed. Splitting Bajinya's ~20% share between his UK legal name 'Vincent Brown' (11%) and birth name 'Vincent Bajinya' (9%) reflects CPS charging announcement naming conventions while leaving 19% for Munyaneza and unnamed suspects.

questions.title: Which country will become the 75th signatory of the Artemis Accords by September 27, 2026?
questions.background: The Artemis Accords establish principles for international cooperation in civil space exploration.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements from NASA or the U.S. Department of State, or contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera. Resolution : Resolve to the country that becomes the 75th signatory of the Artemis Accords on or before September 27, 2026. A completed signing is required; an expression of interest or an intention to sign does not qualify. A signing after that deadline does not count. Accepted Answer Format : The country's name.

Reaching #75 by September 27 (coinciding with UNGA High-Level Week) requires eight additional signings from 40+ plausible non-signatory U.S.-aligned states, so predicting which exact country lands specifically on slot #75 is highly diffuse—each leading candidate carries roughly a 4–6% marginal probability, and proper Brier Skill Score optimization requires not inflating top-5 probabilities. Top non-signatory candidates based on regional waves and U.S. space ties include Croatia (the sole remaining EU member state not yet signed), Qatar (following Oman, Jordan, and Morocco in the Arab world), Costa Rica (leading Latin American holdout), Kenya (top East African space partner), and Indonesia (largest ASEAN holdout after Malaysia and the Philippines signed).

questions.title: Which city or region will the DOSB choose in 2026 to represent Germany in bidding for the 2036, 2040 or 2044 Summer Olympics?
questions.background: The DOSB is Germany's national Olympic committee. Its domestic candidate selection is separate from the International Olympic Committee's eventual decision on which country will host the Games.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The DOSB's official selection announcement, as confirmed by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the city or region officially selected during 2026 to represent Germany in bidding for the 2036, 2040 or 2044 Summer Olympics. This concerns Germany's domestic candidate selection, not the eventual international host selection. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the selected city or region.
questions.current_reasoning: Hamburg withdrew from the DOSB German Olympic bid race on May 31, 2026 after voters rejected its referendum 54.9% to 45.1%, leaving exactly three candidates—Munich, Rhine-Ruhr (Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr), and Berlin—ahead of the Sept 26, 2026 DOSB extraordinary assembly in Baden-Baden. Munich is the frontrunner after delivering 66.4% Yes approval on 42% turnout in Oct 2025 alongside 1972 Olympic legacy venues and Bavarian fiscal strength, while Rhine-Ruhr is a close second after winning 66.0% approval across NRW in April 2026 (1.4M votes) with extensive existing stadiums and IOC-member backing. Berlin trails significantly after declining to hold a public referendum and facing 1936 centennial sensitivities.
